concept_definition: a large natural elevation of the Earth's surface rising abruptly from the surrounding level; a large steep hill, usually higher and steeper than a hill
a naturally raised area of land, smaller than a mountain, often with a rounded summit
a low area of land between hills or mountains, often with a river or stream running through it
a naturally flowing body of water, usually freshwater, that moves along a channel from higher to lower elevations and empties into another body of water (such as a sea, lake, or another river).
a large body of fresh or salt water surrounded by land
A vast body of salt water that covers most of the Earth's surface and is divided into major areas such as the Atlantic, Pacific, Indian, Arctic, and Southern Oceans.
A large body of salt water that covers most of the Earth's surface and is partly enclosed by land; one of the principal divisions of the ocean.
A shore of a body of water, especially a sandy or pebbly area by the sea or a lake where people can walk, sunbathe, or swim.
The land along the edge of the sea; the coastline or shore.
A piece of land completely surrounded by water and smaller than a continent.
A piece of land that is surrounded by water on three sides and connected to a larger landmass on the remaining side.
a large area of land that receives very little precipitation and has sparse vegetation, typically characterized by sand or rock and extreme temperature variations
An elevated and flat piece of land that is substantially higher than the surrounding terrain
a deep, narrow valley with steep, often rocky sides, usually carved by a river
a steep rock face, especially at the edge of the sea or a mountain
a natural underground hollow or chamber in rock, typically large enough for a human to enter
a steep descent of a river or stream, where water falls from a height over rocks or a cliff
A large, slow-moving mass of ice formed from compacted snow that flows downhill or spreads outward under its own weight, often shaping the landscape by erosion and deposition.
A mountain or hill with a crater or vent through which molten rock, ash, and gases are or have been erupted from the Earth's crust.
The region of the atmosphere and outer space that appears as a dome over the Earth, seen as the area where clouds, the sun, moon, and stars appear.
A visible mass of tiny water droplets or ice crystals suspended in the atmosphere, typically forming various shapes and often producing precipitation.
Water that falls from clouds in drops; precipitation in the form of liquid water.
Frozen crystalline precipitation that falls from clouds as white flakes, forming a layer on the ground when temperatures are low.
a natural movement of air, especially a perceptible breeze or a flow of air produced by atmospheric pressure differences
a violent weather event characterized by strong winds, often with rain, snow, thunder, or lightning
A thick cloud of tiny water droplets suspended in the air near the ground that reduces visibility.
A measure of how hot or cold something is, typically determined by a thermometer and expressed in degrees on a standard scale (such as Celsius or Fahrenheit).
a prediction or estimate of future events, especially of weather or economic conditions
a surface with one end higher than the other
a cloud of tiny water droplets in the air
an area of open land, especially one used for cultivation or pasture
The surface of the earth that you stand and walk on.
The outside or top layer of something, including the top of water or land.
a small, narrow river
the land along the edge of a sea, lake, or other large body of water
the land alongside or sloping down to a river or lake
a small body of still water.
a mound of sand formed by the wind.
the bottom of a river channel.
the time when the sun disappears below the horizon.
a hollow place in a solid surface.
a sheltered body of water where ships may anchor safely.
a steady flow of water, air, or electricity in a particular direction.
A series of mountains or hills in a line.
A place where water naturally flows out of the ground.
a connected chain of mountains
a ridge of coral built up in warm shallow sea
a mound of wind-blown sand
a natural spring of warm mineral water
The layer of gases surrounding a planet or other celestial body.
A large rotating storm system with winds spiraling around a low-pressure center; in some regions, especially the Indian Ocean and South Pacific, a tropical cyclone.
A layer surrounding or covering something, especially the Earth beneath the crust or the tissue surrounding an organ.
A ring of light around the sun, moon, or another bright object, caused by reflection or refraction in the atmosphere.
A band of colors or other visible wavelengths produced when light is separated according to wavelength.
A curved band of colored light, usually seen in the sky opposite the sun when sunlight is refracted and reflected by raindrops.
The typical weather conditions of a place over a long period, including temperature, rainfall, and wind.
The highest point of a mountain or hill.
A broad view of natural scenery, especially as seen from a particular place.
Land covered mainly with trees, especially a smaller or less dense area of trees than a forest.
Water that flows over the ground or other surfaces, especially after rain or snowmelt, often carrying soil or pollutants into rivers and lakes.
A narrow passage of water connecting two larger bodies of water.
The boundary where land meets the sea; the outline or strip of land along a coast.
A river or stream that flows into a larger river, lake, or other body of water.
The place where two or more rivers, streams, or other flowing bodies of water meet and join.
The amount of snow that falls during a particular time or storm.
The line where a body of water meets the land; the edge of a sea, lake, river, or other water body.
A powerful stellar explosion in which a star suddenly becomes vastly brighter and then gradually fades, often leaving behind a neutron star or black hole.
Molten or partly molten rock beneath the Earth's surface, from which igneous rocks form when it cools.
The rigid outer layer of Earth, consisting of the crust and the uppermost solid mantle, and lying above the softer asthenosphere.
A mass of air, water, or another fluid that spins rapidly around a central point, often forming a whirling column or spiral.
A dense tropical forest, especially one with thick tangled vegetation.
A long, narrow passage through which water flows, especially a natural or artificial waterway.
A series of rounded bumps on a ski slope, or a freestyle skiing event in which competitors ski over them.
A large area covered chiefly with trees and undergrowth; a woodland ecosystem.
A distinctive natural arrangement of rock, or a group of rock layers.
The region of ozone in Earth's stratosphere that absorbs much of the Sun's ultraviolet radiation.
A natural accumulation or layer of shale rock, especially one considered as a geological formation or source of hydrocarbons.
The elements are the forces of weather and nature, especially when they expose people to harsh or dangerous conditions.
The streams, springs, or small rivers at the upper end of a river system from which a larger river begins.
The natural world, especially the air, water, land, and living things affected by human activity.
One of Earth's major continuous landmasses, conventionally counted as one of seven: Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Europe, North America, Australia, or South America.
Solid, dry ground, especially land as opposed to the sea or air.
A natural or artificial lake or other place where water is collected and stored, especially for supplying a community or for irrigation.
A light, gentle wind.
Rain that falls from the atmosphere, considered as a weather condition or event.
A long, smooth wave in the sea, especially one that continues after the wind that formed it has weakened or stopped.
A small natural stream of water.
The highest point or peak of a wave, ridge, or other rising feature.
Moisture made of tiny drops of water that forms on cool surfaces, especially outdoors, when water vapor in the air condenses.
Frozen precipitation that falls as small balls or lumps of ice.
An impressive or unusual sight or scene that attracts attention.
An upward slope or path, especially one that is difficult to climb.
The upper layer of branches and leaves formed by trees in a forest.
A reef or mass formed from the hard skeletons of coral animals.
A prolonged period of unusually low rainfall that causes a shortage of water, often harming crops, ecosystems, or water supplies.
A ridge of rock, sand, or coral at or near the surface of the sea that can be dangerous to ships.
A long, narrow raised area of land, especially a high line of hills or mountains.
A large area of land that is wild, natural, and not used or changed much by people.
A small natural stream of water, smaller than a river.
A broad area of open, uncultivated land, often wet and covered with rough grasses, heather, or low shrubs.
A large open area of mostly flat or gently rolling grassland, especially the natural grasslands of central North America.
A tract of open, usually treeless grassland, particularly one maintained or restored as a natural habitat, whether or not it is in North America.
A narrow opening, split, or crack, especially one in a rock or in the ground.
A violent tropical storm with very strong rotating winds, typically forming over the Atlantic or eastern Pacific and having sustained winds of at least 74 miles per hour.
A deep, narrow valley with steep sides, usually formed by erosion from flowing water.
A level strip of ground cut into or built onto a slope, often used for farming or to create a flat area.
A very strong, fast-moving stream of water or another liquid.
The universe, or the world regarded as something brought into existence by a creator.
A large group or chain of islands, especially one scattered across a sea or ocean.
A low, often roughly triangular area of land formed by sediment at the mouth of a river, where it divides into smaller channels.
A seasonal wind system that reverses direction during the year, especially one that brings heavy rain to South Asia and nearby regions.
A period of heavy seasonal rain, especially in South Asia and other regions affected by monsoon winds.
A tropical or subtropical grassland with scattered trees and shrubs, typically found in regions with seasonal rainfall.
A community of living organisms, together with the nonliving parts of their environment, interacting as a system.
The geological features, structure, and history of a particular region, planet, or other body.
Water or ice that falls from the atmosphere to the ground, including rain, snow, sleet, or hail.
A body of water partly enclosed by land and connected to a larger body of water.
A sudden shaking of the ground caused by movement in the Earth's crust or by volcanic activity.
A period or condition of freezing weather, especially one that can damage plants.
The open, level grasslands of the central and western United States, especially the Great Plains.
A sheltered place on the coast where ships can anchor or take refuge; a port.
A dense forest in a tropical or subtropical region, characterized by heavy rainfall and abundant plant and animal life.
The natural features of a place, such as hills, forests, and rivers, especially when viewed as attractive.
A prominent or easily recognized feature of a landscape or place, often used to identify or navigate to it.
The apparent line where the earth or sea seems to meet the sky.
A hole or cavity in the ground or in a surface.
The sky or the space above the earth, especially as it appears vast, beautiful, or celestial.
The pointed top or highest part of a mountain or hill.
A large area of sea that is partly enclosed by land.
A low-lying area of land that is very wet, often covered with water and thick vegetation.
An overflow of water that covers land that is normally dry.
